documents.title: Physical results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Happy new year Derek. Your urine microalbumin from the physical came back normal, and the kidney panel is fine. A1c 6.5 is right where we want it on metformin. See you in the summer.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up: Lipids and Medication Adherence
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Back to go over cholesterol and make sure the meds are working for him. Summer break started. No new symptoms of any kind. Takes metformin twice a day and lisinopril every morning, rarely misses.

Family history reviewed again: father with type 2 diabetes diagnosed at 58; mother with hypertension and high cholesterol; maternal grandfather had an MI at 65.
Nonsmoker. Weekend drinks, one or two.

BP 132/84.

Fasting labs from this morning: A1c 7.2% (up from 6.5 in December), glucose 154. TC 210, LDL 140, HDL 40, triglycerides 250.

Assessment
- Mixed hyperlipidemia: LDL and triglycerides both up, HDL low. Adding to the problem list.
- T2DM, A1c drifted up over six months.
- HTN stable on lisinopril.

Plan: we talked about cutting back refined carbs and the weekend beer, more walking now that school is out. I'll send him the dietitian handout. Same metformin and lisinopril. Recheck labs before a visit around the holidays.

documents.title: Eating plan handout
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: As promised, attached is the handout on carbohydrate portions and triglycerides. The big levers for you are sweet drinks, white bread and pasta portions, and beer. We'll recheck everything in December.

documents.title: Re: Eating plan handout
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Got it, thanks. Already switched to seltzer. Eye doctor is booked for October this year.

documents.title: Nurse Visit - Vaccines
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Flu vaccine L deltoid and Moderna bivalent booster R deltoid. Denies fever today. Observed 15 minutes. Says he saw the eye doctor last week and was told all is well; will ask them to fax the report.

documents.title: Lab Draw
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Fasting since 9 pm. Venipuncture R antecubital, one attempt. Urine sample collected. Visit with PCP on 12/26.

events.reason: Follow-up; question about a lipid drug trial

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit - Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
53 y/o with HTN, T2DM, mixed hyperlipidemia. Feels well, nothing new to report. Compliant with metformin and lisinopril.

His main question today: a colleague forwarded him an ad for a study of an investigational cholesterol drug, randomized against placebo, and he wants to know if it is worth his time.

BP 132/84. Exam unremarkable: heart and lungs normal, abdomen benign, legs without swelling.

Labs 12/19 reviewed: A1c 7.2%, fasting glucose 154. TC 210, LDL 130, HDL 40, TG 250. Urine microalbumin normal.

Discussion re trial: went over what placebo-controlled means, that he might get the inactive pill for the length of the study, and what randomization protects against. Pointed out that the planned enrollment is small, so a single study like this can't tell us much on its own, though his participation would still be voluntary and closely monitored. Suggested he read the consent carefully and bring questions to the study team; happy to look at the consent with him. He will think it over.

Plan: same medications. Keep working on diet and walking. Physical in the spring or summer.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Yearly exam. Doing well. No chest discomfort, shortness of breath, numbness in the feet, or vision change. Meds: metformin 1000 mg twice daily, lisinopril 20 mg daily.

Eye exam: went in October, no report ever reached us. He'll ask them again.

Exam: vitals reviewed. Pleasant, fit-appearing. Oropharynx clear, no adenopathy. Heart regular without murmur or gallop. Lungs clear to bases. Abdomen soft. Lower legs without swelling. Foot check: sensation normal to filament, pulses 2+, no skin breakdown.

PHQ-2 = 0.

Plan:
- Labs today: CMP, CBC, lipids, A1c, urine microalbumin.
- Pneumococcal: PCV20 today given diabetes.
- Colonoscopy 2019 normal, next 2029.
- Same meds. Diabetes check in about 6 months.

documents.title: Physical labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Derek, results from yesterday are in. Kidney and liver tests, blood count and urine protein are all normal. A1c is about the same as December. Enjoy the summer.

documents.title: Diabetic Eye Exam Report
documents.author: optometry
documents.body:
Exam 9/12/2023 at our office. Patient with type 2 diabetes for routine dilated examination.
Best corrected acuity 20/20 each eye. Pressures normal.
Anterior segments quiet. Lenses clear.
Dilated retinal exam: no microaneurysms, dot-blot hemorrhages, cotton wool spots or edema in either eye. Optic nerves healthy.
Impression: no diabetic retinopathy. See in one year.

documents.title: Nurse Visit - Fall Vaccines
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Influenza IM L arm, updated Moderna COVID IM R arm. Both tolerated. Diabetes follow-up booked for 12/12.

documents.title: Missed Appointment
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Did not arrive for 3:40 visit. Called, he apologized, had parent conferences run late and forgot to cancel. Rebooked for January 11.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Diabetes Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Rescheduled from December. Nothing new. No lows, no thirst, no foot symptoms. Lisinopril and metformin unchanged.
Optometry letter from September: no retinopathy.
Exam: vitals ok. Cardiopulmonary exam normal. Feet intact.
Plan: A1c and BMP today. Continue. Physical in July.

documents.title: Results
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Hi Derek, your doctor reviewed yesterday's labs: kidney function and potassium normal, A1c filed for your physical in July. No medication changes.

documents.title: Pharmacy Refill Request
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Electronic refill request from his pharmacy for metformin 1000 mg #180 and lisinopril 20 mg #90. Seen in January, labs fine. Approved both with 3 refills.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Here for yearly physical. Summer school teaching, otherwise relaxing. Feels good. Same two medications, taken reliably. NKDA. Still never smoked, still a couple of drinks on the weekend.

Review of systems is negative.

Vitals in range. Exam: alert, well. Eyes, ears, throat normal. Neck supple, thyroid not enlarged. Heart sounds normal, no murmur. Breath sounds clear. Abdomen nontender, no masses. Extremities warm, no swelling. Diabetic foot exam normal. Mood and affect normal, PHQ-2 0.

Plan: CMP, lipids, A1c, urine microalbumin today. Immunizations current; flu and COVID in the fall. Colonoscopy due 2029. Return in 6 months for diabetes.

documents.title: Nurse Visit - Vaccines
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Trivalent flu L deltoid and 2024-25 COVID (Pfizer) R deltoid. No prior reactions apart from a tired day after his second Moderna in 2021. Fine after observation. He has not booked his eye exam yet this year; reminder given.
